newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sugar looks soft after NY May expiry.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sugar looks soft after NY May expiry.

text.p: LIFFE sugar was softer on Thursday after the May expiry in New York, traders said.
By 1055 GMT front month August, which has dominated volume, was 90 cents lower at $309.50. Of the total 538 lots traded so far, 448 were on August.
"We saw more South Brazilian sugar come to the tape than had been expected," one trader said. "It shows that the availability is more than expected in the short term."
Whites had largely kept in line with raws, he said. Despite the soft look to the market, he was looking for August to hold above $308.00.
New York world sugar futures settled sharply lower in May as the Brazilians were reported to have stepped in to sell the contract ahead of its expiry, market sources there said.
"The Brazilians were waiting to hit it; it looks like they are going to deliver," Peter Perez, a sugar broker with Merrill Lynch, said.
